overview: The Medford Energy and Environment Committee met to review municipal climate projects, draft tree ordinances, and new member recruitment. The committee also discussed waste reduction initiatives, co-chair leadership for the upcoming year, and meeting schedules.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Administrative Updates and Co-Chair Leadership
items.summary: The committee discussed filling co-chair leadership positions, with members agreeing to hold formal leadership votes at the January meeting.

items.title: New Member Recruitment and Committee Priorities
items.summary: Staff updated the committee on four candidate applicants for two open seats, prompting a discussion on focus areas including composting, zero waste, and single-use plastics reduction.

items.title: Climate Policy and Municipal Project Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike updated the committee on various municipal initiatives, including Electrify Medford community events, school HVAC upgrades, school bus electrification planning, and the hazard mitigation plan update.

items.title: Trees Medford and Draft Tree Ordinances Update
items.summary: Lauretta James reported on a City Council Committee of the Whole meeting regarding proposed tree ordinances, noting the council passed a motion to continue revising the language with city departments.

items.title: Waste Reduction Outreach and Climate Bill Discussion
items.summary: The committee agreed to postpone a state climate bill presentation to January and discussed reaching out to neighboring communities regarding zero waste programs.

items.title: New Business and Rodenticide Advocacy Update
items.summary: Lauretta James provided an update on state-level public engagement regarding the impacts of rodenticides on local wildlife.
